title: Trifle
subtitle: Layers of sponge, jelly, custard, and cream
excerpt: Sponge fingers soaked in sherry and fruit jelly, layered with thick vanilla custard and topped with softly whipped double cream. The definitive British celebration dessert.

recipe.sourceNotes: Trifle has been a centrepiece of British dessert tables since at least the 18th century. The name derives from the archaic English word 'trifle', meaning something light and of little consequence — ironic given how elaborate the dish has become. Early trifles were simple cream dishes; the layered construction with sponge, jelly, custard, and cream emerged in the Victorian era. The use of sherry to soak the sponge is traditional and distinguishes a proper trifle from a quick assembly. A trifle made entirely from scratch, including homemade custard and jelly, is markedly better than one assembled from packet ingredients.

content.text: Each layer must be fully set or cool before the next is added, or the layers will bleed into each other. Make the jelly first, arrange the sponge and sherry, pour over the jelly, and chill until completely set before adding the custard. The custard must be cooled to room temperature before it goes on the jelly, otherwise it will melt through. Decorate the trifle just before serving.
Arrange the sponge fingers in the base of a large trifle bowl or glass dish. Pour the sherry over them. Scatter half the raspberries over the top.
Make the jelly to packet instructions and leave to cool for 10 minutes. Pour gently over the sponge layer. Refrigerate for at least 2 hours until completely set.

Make the custard: whisk the egg yolks, sugar, and cornflour together. Heat the milk and 200 ml cream with the vanilla until steaming. Pour onto the egg mixture, whisking constantly. Return to the pan and stir over medium heat until thick. Cover the surface with cling film and cool to room temperature.
Pour the cooled custard over the set jelly. Refrigerate for 1 hour.
Whip the 400 ml cream with the icing sugar to soft peaks. Spoon over the custard. Decorate with the remaining raspberries and toasted flaked almonds. Serve at once or refrigerate for up to 4 hours.
